text: In eighteen forty-nine, a little girl stood on a leaf.
It held her.
The leaf belonged to a giant Amazon water lily.
And the man who grew it was her father, Joseph Paxton.
A gardener. The first to make it bloom in England.
Turn the leaf over, and you see why it's so strong.
Ribs. Spreading the weight in every direction.
A year later, London had a problem.
It was hosting the Great Exhibition, and needed a building.
Two hundred and forty-five designs had been submitted.
Every one was rejected.
So in a railway meeting, Paxton picked up a pen...
and sketched an idea on blotting paper.
A building made like that leaf.
Iron ribs. Glass panes. Every part made in a factory.
Experts warned it would collapse.
So soldiers marched across the galleries to test it.
It held.
On the first of May, eighteen fifty-one, the Crystal Palace opened.
Nearly three hundred thousand panes of glass.
Six million visitors.
Every glass building since owes something to that leaf.
